newsitem.title: HAITI: U.S. security agents guard Haiti National Palace.
newsitem.headline: U.S. security agents guard Haiti National Palace.

text.p: U.S. security agents were guarding Haiti's Presidential Palace on Saturday, following allegations President Rene Preval's security officers were involved in recent assassinations of opposition politicians.
The 40 State Department diplomatic security agents were deployed swiftly and quietly on Friday in what U.S. embassy spokeswoman Meg Gilroy described as a training exercise.
"The unit will be doing training in VIP protection," she said. "President Preval has announced he wants to reorganize Palace security."
Preval told Joseph Moise, the head of the 87-agent security team, and his deputy Milien Romage that they were being transferred, according to palace security personnel.
State Department officials said further purgings within the unit were in the works, to be carried out while the diplomatic security agents remained at the palace.
Gilroy said the State Department security team may remain at the palace for several months.
The plan to reorganize Preval's security was the focus of an emergency meeting on Aug. 30 at the residence of U.S. Ambassador William Lacey Swing.
The meeting was attended by Preval, National Security Adviser Anthony Lake, Dep. Secretary of State Strobe Talbott as well as high-level Canadian officials.

U.S. embassy officials informed Preval that the State Department had evidence linking Preval's security unit to the Aug. 20 double assassination of a leader and a member of the Mobilisation for National Development (MDN) party.

The MDN is associated with the disbanded Haitian military, which was widely believed to have attacked the Port-au-Prince police station and Parliament building with automatic weapons and grenades the night before the assassinations.

U.S. embassy and United Nations sources fear the assassinations of Pastor Antoine Leroy, the number two in the MDN, and party member Jacques Florival may have been a retaliatory act by loose-cannon forces in the ruling Lavalas party.
"Moise and others within Preval's security see themselves as the true protectors of Lavalas," said a Western diplomat.
Palace security agents were approved by former president, and Preval's close friend, Jean-Bertrand Aristide during his exile in the United States after a 1991 military coup.
Shortly after he was returned by U.S. troops in 1994, Aristide disbanded the military.
Former soldiers angry at no longer receiving a pension or pay demanded compensation or threatened to use violence.
The U.S. embassy informed Preval in July of a plot to assassinate him. Shortly afterwards U.S. troops began monthly training exercises in Haiti, in part as a show of force.
